sensitivity_null_tradeoff.description: Monotonic tradeoff: decreasing alpha increases K3 sensitivity but degrades null centering
sensitivity_null_tradeoff.crossover_alpha: none (no alpha achieves both C1 and C3)

C1-NULL-CONTROL.description: Shuffled-action within-session null, 500 permutations per alpha. |mean| < 0.1 bits.
C1-NULL-CONTROL.expected: |shuffled-action null_mean| < 0.1 bits for at least one alpha
C1-NULL-CONTROL.observed: Only alpha=1.0 passes (|mean|=0.064). Alpha=0: 0.924, alpha=0.01: 0.941, alpha=0.1: 0.561, alpha=0.5: 0.151.

C3-POSITIVE-CONTROL.description: Positive control K3 >= 0.5 bits with permutation p <= 0.001 for any alpha passing C1.
C3-POSITIVE-CONTROL.observed: Alpha=1.0 (C1 passer) has K3=0.099 < 0.5. Alphas 0, 0.01, 0.1 pass C3 but fail C1.

B-DETERMINISTIC-SPA.description: Plug-in KL on fully deterministic SPA. Expected I(Y;A|Z)=0 by construction.
B-DETERMINISTIC-SPA.observed: K3 values: alpha=0: 1.391, alpha=0.01: 1.294, alpha=0.1: 0.773, alpha=0.5: 0.239, alpha=1.0: 0.109. All > 0.1 due to Laplace smoothing bias.

observations: Strong monotonic sensitivity-null tradeoff: alpha=0 K3=1.377 bits but |null_mean|=0.924 (9.2x threshold); alpha=1.0 |null_mean|=0.064 (1.6x below threshold) but K3=0.099 (5.1x below 0.5 threshold).
No alpha achieves BOTH C1 (|null_mean|<0.1) AND C3 (K3>=0.5). The crossover does not exist in the tested alpha range.
C1 passers: {1.0} only. C3 passers: {0, 0.01, 0.1}. Intersection: empty.

The null bias is intrinsic to plug-in KL estimation across varying-size strata: it decreases monotonically with alpha (0.924 at alpha=0 to 0.064 at alpha=1.0) because Laplace smoothing dilutes the per-stratum PMI contribution.
Sensitivity (K3 on stochastic SPA) decreases monotonically with alpha: 1.377 (alpha=0) -> 1.274 (0.01) -> 0.743 (0.1) -> 0.221 (0.5) -> 0.099 (1.0).

The degenerate control (deterministic SPA, I=0 by construction) is non-zero for all alphas due to Laplace smoothing bias: alpha=0: 1.391, alpha=0.01: 1.294, alpha=0.1: 0.773, alpha=0.5: 0.239, alpha=1.0: 0.109.
Stratum size decomposition (alpha=0.1): 343 strata in 5-9 bucket (observed PMI 0.800, null 0.644), 37 strata in 10-19 bucket (observed 0.961, null 0.616). Smaller strata have higher null bias.
Determinism ratio K3=9.2% (77 deterministic / 841 total strata), confirming the stochastic SPA has substantial non-determinism.
Parent audit MLE recomputation (alpha=0 K3=1.377, alpha=0.1 K3=0.743) is exactly replicated in this experiment.
Permutation p-value is identical (0.001) across all alphas for the positive control, confirming the stochastic SPA signal is detectable by permutation test regardless of alpha.
validity_notes: The experiment uses the same 12-state stochastic SPA design as parent EXP-PHYSICS-35510154353 and EXP-PHYSICS-35482477045. Results are specific to this SPA class.
MLE (alpha=0) handles zero-count cells by skipping them (convention: 0*log2(0/...) = 0). This is mathematically correct for KL divergence but means empty cells contribute zero, not negative bias.
The null control uses within-session action-label shuffle (500 permutations), correcting the global shuffle deviation identified in parent audits.
Bootstrap CI for K3-K2 is NOT computed because no alpha passes both C1 and C3 (Phase 2 not executed).
The stratum size decomposition uses alpha=0.1 as representative; decomposition may differ at other alphas.
All measurements are on synthetic in-memory SPA simulation. No browser/network/model calls. Generalization to production Web transitions is not claimed.
The frozen decision rule FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING triggers on C3 (alpha=1.0 passes C1 but K3=0.099 < 0.5). This is a valid scientific negative, not an infrastructure failure.
unresolved: Whether the sensitivity-null tradeoff is fundamental to discrete CMI estimation or can be broken by (a) larger N, (b) richer state representations, (c) alternative estimators (histogram, Bayesian, likelihood-ratio), or (d) different null frameworks.
Whether the null bias at alpha=0 (0.924 bits) reflects genuine PMI in the shuffled data or estimator artifact from sparse strata (avg 1.5 records per (z,a) cell in K3 conditioning).
Whether K3-K2 beyond-Markov testing is feasible with any plug-in KL alpha given the observed tradeoff.
Whether production Web transitions with continuous state representations or larger vocabularies exhibit different sensitivity-null tradeoffs.
Whether alternative null frameworks (parametric bootstrap, Miller-Madow, conditional entropy) center null at zero for reduced-alpha plug-in KL.
